_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-10-19 — the week the image lane finally got a clean-licensed entrant that is already packaged for the service this box runs, and the week two of this report's own claims had to be withdrawn. Ran on schedule: the previous report is 2026-10-12, a clean seven-day gap. NOTHING WAS ADOPTED — no candidate's checkpoint is in config/model-meta.json, no upgrade's target is in config/ai-router.yaml, and config/wired-models.json has not gained an entry since 2026-09-18, so all seven alias repoints are still one wire-all and one line each. THE NEW THING is Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image: apache-2.0, ungated, 354k downloads in 30 days, a 13.01 GB int8 weight set against the 26 GB local-ming-image was measured at for the same text-heavy job, and JSON layout prompts with bounding boxes that nothing on either machine accepts. Its quality is unmeasured — absent from the Artificial Analysis arena — so it is an evaluate, not an adopt. THE BOARDS BARELY MOVED: the Open ASR Leaderboard shipped two builds (15-10 and 17-10) and, diffed row by row, NO open-weights row changed by a digit; the Open TTS Leaderboard's newest build is still 09-10. TWO CORRECTIONS, both this report's own: Cohere Transcribe is open #10 on clean short-form English and weights-#3 on multilingual, not open #2 and open #1 as the 12-10 entry claimed — it is open #1 on the two boards that matter here, noise and long-form, and remains the pick for a different reason than was given; and Iris-3B's footprint omitted the 8.89 GB Qwen3-VL-4B text encoder its own config names. Iris-3B also gained a 4-step turbo build, which answers the one objection raised against it last week. One new upgrade: Google now publishes a stable flagship, gemini-4-argon, which retires this report's standing reason for leaving gemini-pro pinned to a preview id.

candidates.name: MOSS-Image-SFT (OpenMOSS 5B single-stream DiT)
candidates.params: 5.08B DiT + a separate ~8.4B text encoder the parameter count does not include
candidates.license: apache-2.0 (both the OpenMOSS repos and the Comfy-Org repack; neither is gated)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image file listing, read 19-10, for the THREE FILES A COMFYUI RUN ACTUALLY LOADS at the smallest useful rung: diffusion_models/moss_image_sft_int8_convrot.safetensors 5,413,698,958 B + text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors 7,343,591,088 B + vae/flux2-vae_small.safetensors 249,521,340 B = 13,006,811,386 B. VRAM is that x 1.15 runtime overhead and is NOT a measured peak — ComfyUI streams encoders, so the real peak is probably lower, and activation cost at 2K is unknown. The other rungs, same source: int8 encoder 9,748,121,532 B (15.41 GB set), bf16 DiT 10,164,655,808 B + bf16 encoder 19,306,312,328 B + full flux2-vae 336,211,292 B (29.81 GB set, which is the B5 shape). The ORIGINAL diffusers repo is 27,229 MB over 37 files with its own text_encoder at 16,785,478,992 B — 2.52 GB SMALLER than the file Comfy-Org publishes as qwen3.5_9b_bf16, a packaging difference this run did not resolve and is not claiming to understand. HF reports 5,082,308,624 params BF16, and 5,082,308,624 x 2 = 10,164,617,248 against a 10,164,655,808 B transformer directory, so the published count covers the DiT ONLY and excludes the encoder entirely.

candidates.why: THE WEEK'S ONE REAL FIND, AND THE FIRST IMAGE CANDIDATE THAT ARRIVES ALREADY PACKAGED FOR THE SERVICE BETENSHI RUNS. Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image appeared 16-10 and has 354,126 downloads in 30 days against Comfy-Org/Ming-Image's 176,870 — and every image model in config/model-meta.json except Z-Image and the Draw Things pair is a Comfy-Org repack, so this is a file copy into ComfyUI/models/, not a new service. WHAT IT BEATS HERE, and it is footprint rather than quality: local-ming-image is the installed text-heavy design model, MIT, measured 3 Oct at +23.86 GiB for a 1024 generation and +25.64 GiB for an edit, declared at 26 GB VRAM / 20 GB RAM, and config/model-meta.json records WHY — 'the 19.5 GB int8 Ling-mini-2.0 encoder dominates'. MOSS-Image does the same job with a 7.34 GB w4a8 or 9.75 GB int8 encoder, for a 13.01 GB total weight set: roughly half of Ming's measured peak, and the difference is almost entirely the encoder. Ming 'cannot share the card with vllm-small either way'; a 15 GB MOSS run plausibly can, which on a 31.8 GB card is the whole argument. WHAT IT ADDS that neither box has: JSON LAYOUT PROMPTS — `summary.caption` plus `items` with yxyx bounding boxes in an absolute centred space — so text and object placement are specified rather than hoped for. local-ideogram-4 takes structured JSON captions but not boxes, and nothing on either machine accepts a layout. THE HONEST COST, and docs/models.md rule 5b decides how to say it: THERE IS NO INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT OF THIS MODEL. It is absent from the Artificial Analysis text-to-image arena as of 19-10, where Ming-Image-0.1-Design sits at Elo 999 and Qwen-Image-2.1 at 1042, so no Elo comparison exists in either direction. Its own technical report (arXiv 2610.23374, 16-10) claims state of the art among open-weight models on LongLongTextBench at 96.3% average text coverage and second place end-to-end on RealLayoutArena — but the same paper introduces both benchmarks, so those are vendor numbers on vendor-authored tests, not a board. Eight days old, 2,087 downloads on the diffusers repo, 359 likes. So this is an EVALUATE ON BETENSHI: apache-2.0, ComfyUI-native, half the footprint of the model it would sit beside, and worth 13 GB of disk to find out whether the text rendering holds up against Ming. ON B5 IT IS UNREMARKABLE AND ALSO UNRUNNABLE AS PACKAGED: the 29.81 GB bf16 set is nothing against 128 GB, but config/hosts/b5.json has no comfyui service — B5's image path is Draw Things through the qwen adapter — so taking it there means the diffusers route and a new service, which is a different job from copying three files.

candidates.name: Iris-3B (pixel-space diffusion + depth + upscaler, now with a 4-step turbo build)
candidates.params: 2.99B DiT; the text encoder is Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct and is NOT in this repo
candidates.license: apache-2.0 (repo not gated; the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct encoder it pulls is apache-2.0 too)

requirement.basis: CORRECTED THIS WEEK — last week's 13.7 GB VRAM / 11.95 GB disk COUNTED ONLY THE DENOISER. turbo/config.yaml names `text_encoder: pretrained: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, which the repo does not ship: that is a further 8,887,292,732 B (exact from its own listing, 4.44B params BF16), so no Iris build runs on this repo alone. Disk here is the TURBO set, both figures exact, read 19-10: turbo/model.safetensors 5,975,089,200 B + the encoder's 8,887,292,732 B = 14,862,381,932 B. VRAM is that x 1.15, not measured and not a peak. The FULL build is 11,950,112,680 + 8,887,292,732 = 20,837,405,412 B of weights, 23.96 GB at the same overhead. 5,975,089,200 / 2,987,511,888 = 2.0000 bytes/param against the root's 4.0000, so turbo/ is the bf16 half-precision export that last week said was unpublished. The WHOLE repo is now 41,911,753,317 B over five directories — root 11.950, depth 11.990, upscaler 11.987, turbo 5.975 GB — up from 35.94 GB last week purely because turbo/ is new (repo lastModified 2026-10-12T18:06Z). Still download one directory, never the snapshot.

candidates.why: THE OBJECTION THIS ENTRY WAS RAISED WITH HAS BEEN ANSWERED BY THE AUTHORS, AND ITS FOOTPRINT WAS WRONG. Seven days outstanding (first raised 2026-10-12, read from git). Last week's stated cost was 'CFG 3 at 100 STEPS for a one-megapixel image... expect it to be slower per image than everything installed'. A `turbo/` directory landed hours after that report was written: distill.yaml gives a TDM/DMD decoupled-hybrid distillation with FOUR sigmas — 1.0, 0.938, 0.833, 0.625 — at CFG 3.5 and 1024x1024, which is a 4-step model, a 25x step reduction, and it is half the size at bf16 rather than fp32. That puts it in the same class as Z-Image-Turbo and FLUX.2-klein-4B, which is where the image lane's few-step models already are. AND THE CORRECTION, stated here rather than quietly fixed: the 11.95 GB this report has been quoting since 12-10 is the denoiser alone. Iris encodes text with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, pulled separately, 8.89 GB — so the real turbo set is 14.86 GB and the real full set 20.84 GB. Both still fit BeTenshi's 31.8 GB card; the full one at ~24 GB runs alone and blocks every other image model, which 13.7 GB did not imply. WHAT IT STILL ADDS, unchanged and still the reason it is here: the same pixel-space prior ships as monocular DEPTH ESTIMATION (depth/, 11.99 GB) and image RESTORATION/UPSCALING (upscaler/, 11.99 GB), fine-tuned without architectural change, and nothing on BeTenshi or B5 does depth or super-resolution at all. It has no VAE — the network emits every pixel. STILL NO MEASURED QUALITY: absent from the Artificial Analysis arena as of 19-10, so this is licence and capability, not Elo. Adoption is still negligible and now readable as a trend: 1,450 downloads in the last 30 days against 393 at the 12-10 read, 313 likes, two weeks old. SECOND PRIORITY TO MOSS-IMAGE ON BETENSHI for one reason only — Iris has no ComfyUI packaging, so it needs a service written, where MOSS-Image is three files into a directory. Unremarkable in B5's pool, and the same no-ComfyUI caveat applies there.

candidates.why: STILL THE PICK FOR BETENSHI, BUT TWO OF LAST WEEK'S THREE RANKING CLAIMS WERE WRONG AND ARE WITHDRAWN HERE. 56 days outstanding (first raised 2026-08-24, read from git). BeTenshi has served stt from whisper-large-v3 on :8001 throughout. WHAT WAS CLAIMED LAST WEEK: open #1 on three of four boards and open #2 on clean short-form English 'behind only Qwen3-ASR'. WHAT THE 17-10 CSVs SAY, cross-joined on the eight clean datasets every row shares: Cohere's 4.670 is open #10, not #2 — Qwen3-ASR 4.311, Hojo-ASR-V1 4.334, higgs-audio-v3-stt 4.392, canary-qwen-2.5b 4.428, ARK-ASR-3B 4.475, thewhisper-large-v3-turbo 4.539, ARK-ASR-0.6B 4.559, granite-speech-4.1-2b 4.615 and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 4.636 all come first. And on multilingual it is weights-#3 at 3.842, behind thewhisper-large-v3-turbo 3.613 and Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 3.745, not #1. Every one of those numbers was available on the 09-10 build this report read last week; the error was comparing Cohere against whisper and Qwen3-ASR alone and calling the result a field ranking. This report's own notes contradicted its own `why` field, which is how it was caught. WHAT SURVIVES IS STILL ENOUGH TO PICK IT, and it is the two boards that describe a microphone in a room. URGENT2024, degraded and noisy speech: Cohere is open #1 at 9.50, against whisper's 13.73 — a 31% relative error reduction — and only three models on the whole board beat it, all proprietary APIs (zoom/scribe_v2_pro 7.99, OtterAI/speech-v3.1 8.07, assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro 9.08). LONG-FORM, meetings and earnings calls: open #1 at 9.733 against whisper's 11.228, with the next open model parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 at 10.72. Both at 923.71 RTFx against whisper's 470.73, for a 4.13 GB download. The models that beat it on clean English lose on one or both: Qwen3-ASR is 9.93 on noise and ABSENT from long-form, Hojo is 12.33 on noise at 73 RTFx, MOSS is 12.74. Its 14 declared languages include ARABIC, which this box has a harness for (config/arabic-eval.json, docs/arabic-model-experiment-2026-09-14.md) and which no board measures and no other candidate covers. UNREMARKABLE ON B5, which has run an 8-bit MLX Qwen3-ASR build since 20-09 and has the pool for anything here. The caveat is unchanged: `gated: auto` under apache-2.0, a click-through a human accepts once. 120,580 downloads in the last 30 days and 3,473,528 all-time.

candidates.why: THE SHORT-ENGLISH SPECIALIST FOR BETENSHI, AND NOW THE CLEAN-BOARD LEADER OUTRIGHT. 61 days outstanding (first raised 2026-08-19, read from git). In service on B5 since 20-09 as `qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit`, so this speaks only to BeTenshi, where :8001 is still whisper-large-v3. On the eight clean datasets every row shares it is open #1 at 4.311 against whisper's 5.780 — a 25% relative reduction — at 835.62 RTFx against 470.73. The ranking caveat from last week still holds and still matters: its POSTED average is 5.746, which reads as mid-table, because the board's `avg` column spans a different number of datasets per row (Phi-4-multimodal's covers eight, Cohere's seven, OtterAI's nine) and cannot be compared across rows at all. Read the per-dataset columns, not the headline. WHERE IT LOSES, unchanged: multilingual 5.525 against whisper's 4.566 — worse than the model it would replace on five of the six measured languages despite 52 advertised — and ABSENT from the long-form board, so nothing is known about a meeting recording. On URGENT2024 it is 9.93, open #2, 0.43 behind Cohere. So Cohere remains the general pick and this stays the narrow one: take it on BeTenshi only if that box transcribes short English utterances and nothing else, which is what voice input in the Studio is. Four weeks in service on B5 is evidence it runs, not evidence it is right for the other box. 373,717 downloads in the last 30 days, 869,009 all-time.

candidates.name: AuK-Flash (Tencent Hunyuan speech foundation model, distilled)
candidates.params: the Open TTS Leaderboard records 1.53B; HF publishes no count and the repo ships 6.76 GB, so the count is still not the footprint

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 19-10 and byte-for-byte unchanged: auk_flash.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + vae.safetensors 637,322,604 B = 6,759,531,696 B of weights, 6,762,657,045 B for the whole repo; lastModified still 2026-09-09. HF publishes NO parameter count for either AuK repo and the safetensors index carries no dtype summary, so estimateFromParams() must not be used on them — the leaderboard's 1.53B against 6.76 GB would be 4.4 bytes/param, so that figure describes one component. VRAM is 6.76 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured. At 6.76 GB the weight set fits BeTenshi's card outright, so unlike the image models it needs no CPU offload and holds no standing host-RAM cost. Benchmarks are the Open TTS Leaderboard build 09-10-2026, re-pulled 19-10 through the Space's own _refresh_leaderboard endpoint because hf-audio/tts_leaderboard_results still returns 401 to an anonymous fetch; 09-10 is still the newest entry in the Space's version dropdown, so the board has not moved in a week.

candidates.why: UNCHANGED, AND RE-VERIFIED RATHER THAN CARRIED OVER. 28 days outstanding (first raised 2026-09-21, read from git). On CV3-Eval English in cloning mode — the one dataset and language where this model and the service running on :8004 are both scored — AuK-Flash is 3.35 WER / 72.67 SIM / 26.61 RTFx against ChatterboxMultilingualTTS's 4.43 / 53.13 / 0.99, identical to three decimals to both earlier reads. That is +19.5 speaker-similarity points on the one axis a cloning service exists for, 24% lower word error, and 27x the throughput, under the same MIT licence. config/model-meta.json confirms local-chatterbox IS the Multilingual variant, so that is the right comparison, not the English-only sibling. AuK and AuK-Flash still hold the top two SIM scores of any model on the CV3 English cloning board at 73.00 and 72.67, ahead of k2-fsa/OmniVoice (70.05, cc-by-nc) and openbmb/VoxCPM2 (69.02). Take Flash, not the base: same 6.76 GB, 0.11 WER worse, 6x the speed. THE COST, plainly and unchanged: AuK-Flash declares zh and en only, where Chatterbox declares 23 including Arabic, and no board measures Arabic. So this is an ADDITION for English and Chinese, not a repoint of :8004 — and a new service to write, because AuK is an instruction-driven pipeline that also does speech editing, enhancement and source separation, which nothing on either box can do. THE ALTERNATIVE WORTH WEIGHING FIRST, and it is apache-2.0 rather than MIT: openbmb/VoxCPM2 is 2.67 WER / 69.02 SIM on the same board with 30 declared languages against AuK's 2 — better intelligibility and far better breadth for 3.65 fewer similarity points — and it is ruled out here only on speed, at 1.79 RTFx against 26.61, a 15x gap that decides it for anything interactive. On BeTenshi 6.76 GB sits on the card beside Kokoro's 0.4 GB and Chatterbox's measured 3.0 GB without disturbing either; unremarkable on B5. Adoption is still thin and this report should keep saying so: 1,438 downloads in 30 days, 3,820 all-time — DOWN from 2,963 in 30 days a week ago.

candidates.why: THE NON-ENGLISH READING VOICE FOR BETENSHI, unchanged and re-confirmed on a board that did not move. 56 days outstanding (first raised 2026-08-24, read from git). In service on B5 since 20-09 as `qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice`, so this speaks only to BeTenshi. DO NOT REPOINT :8002 AT IT: on the English no-cloning board (Seed-TTS + CV3) Kokoro-82M is 1.46 average WER at 71.15 RTFx against this model's 1.71 at 13.32, so for reading English aloud the 82M model already installed is faster, more intelligible and a fortieth of the size. WHAT SURVIVES IS BREADTH, and it is a real gap. Across all nine languages CV3-Eval measures, this model ranks 3rd at 4.22 average WER; Kokoro is unranked because it has no German, Korean or Russian at all, and the multilingual voice this box gained on 18-09 — Chatterbox — ranks 10th at 11.28. Per language, reading without cloning: German 5.96 against Chatterbox's 17.45, French 5.94 against 16.34, Russian 5.70 against 13.49, Japanese 5.90 against 8.82. All identical to the 18-09 and 09-10 reads. So if BeTenshi needs to read non-English text aloud this is the model, it beats what shipped on 18-09 by two to three times on error, and B5 has already made that call for itself. The correction from three weeks ago stands and is re-confirmed: the board records CustomVoice as NOT supporting voice cloning — 'CustomVoice' is a speaker bank. The `-Base` sibling is the cloner, 3rd on the CV3 English cloning board at 2.85 WER / 66.96 SIM and 3rd across nine languages at 4.07 / 72.60. Downloads by metric, as docs/models.md requires: 2,120,221 in the last 30 days, 17,205,603 all-time.

upgrades.why: NEW THIS WEEK, AND IT RETIRES THIS REPORT'S OWN STANDING REASON FOR NOT TOUCHING THIS ALIAS. Every earlier run recorded that gemini-pro stays pinned to gemini-3.1-pro-preview ON PURPOSE because Google published no stable Pro-tier model to move to. As of the 19-10 read that is no longer true: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models now carries a GEMINI 4 section whose one entry, gemini-4-argon, is labelled stable and described as 'Our flagship reasoning model, built for complex software engineering, deep mathematical and scientific problem solving'. THE PRICE MAKES IT UNAMBIGUOUS, from the published pricing page the same day: gemini-4-argon is $2.00 / $10.00 per 1M input/output on the paid standard tier (promotional through 30 November 2026; $4.00 / $20.00 from 1 December), against gemini-3.1-pro-preview's $2.00 / $12.00 for prompts up to 200k and $4.00 / $18.00 above it. So this is the same input price, a 17% cut on output, and a move off a PREVIEW id onto a stable one — the thing the pin was waiting for. After 1 December the promotional price ends and argon's $4.00 / $20.00 is dearer than the preview's small-prompt tier, so the comparison is worth re-reading then rather than assuming it holds. NO DEADLINE IS CLAIMED: gemini-3.1-pro-preview is still published and still the newest model in the Pro line, which is a line argon does not belong to; nothing is broken today. PREREQUISITE: no gemini-4 id appears in config/wired-models.json, whose newest entries are all dated 2026-09-18, so run the console's Wire all first, then edit the one line.

SEVEN DAYS OUTSTANDING (first raised 2026-10-12, read from git), AND THE DATE IT WAS RAISED ABOUT HAS NOW PASSED — SO THE PREDICTION CAN BE SCORED. Last week this entry said the 15 October retirement commitment on claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 was a guaranteed-availability floor and not a deprecation, that nothing would break on the day, and that Anthropic promises at least 60 days' notice. Re-read 19-10, four days after: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 is STILL LISTED ACTIVE on the deprecations page, with the same 'Not sooner than October 15, 2026' text and no deprecation date. That was the right call, and it is now a fact rather than a forecast. WHAT HAS CHANGED IS THE OTHER PAGE: the models overview now lists Claude Haiku 4.5 under 'Legacy models (still available)', alongside Opus 5, Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 4.6 — so all three Claude aliases in this router point at models Anthropic itself labels legacy, which is a stronger and more current argument than the retirement date ever was. The floor having expired with the model still Active means a notice can now arrive at any time, with 60 days to act; this is the one alias in the file where that is true. claude-haiku-5-5 is Active, current, with a floor of October 7, 2027, and the overview prices it from $0.10 / $0.50 per 1M input/output against Sonnet 5.5's $2.00 / $10.00. PREREQUISITE, shared with the next two entries: claude-haiku-5-5 is NOT in config/wired-models.json. Run Wire all, then edit the alias — one click and one restart, then one line by hand.

SIXTY-ONE DAYS OUTSTANDING — first raised 2026-08-19, read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json`, not incremented from last week's 'fifty-four'. The target is confirmed for a second week and is now corroborated by a second page. claude-opus-5-5 is the current Opus: the models overview names it the default recommendation 'for most workloads' at $4.00 / $20.00 per 1M input/output, and lists BOTH the wired claude-opus-4-8 AND claude-opus-5 — the target this report recommended until 28-09 — under 'Legacy models (still available)'. So the wired model is two generations behind and last week's target is one, exactly as stated then, and the vendor's own lifecycle wording now says so rather than this report inferring it from retirement dates. Retirement commitments give the ordering: opus-5-5 not sooner than 2027-09-22, opus-5 2027-07-24, opus-4-8 2027-05-28. NO DEADLINE IS CLAIMED: the deprecations table lists all three as Active with no deprecation date, so this is a capability and currency argument, not a retirement one. claude-opus-5-5 is NOT wired, so this needs a wire-all before the alias edit; claude-opus-5 has had its own alias since the 08-19 sweep and is not the thing to point at.

SIXTY-ONE DAYS OUTSTANDING, dated from git, and the same two-page confirmation as claude-opus. claude-sonnet-5-5 is the current Sonnet — 'the best combination of speed and intelligence' on the models overview at $2.00 / $10.00 per 1M tokens, retirement floor 2027-09-28 — while the wired claude-sonnet-4-6 AND claude-sonnet-5, the target this report carried until 05-10, are both now under 'Legacy models (still available)'. The wired claude-sonnet-4-6 dates from 2026-02-17, making this still the most stale alias in the file at just over eight months. THE IMAGE LANE'S BIGGEST RELEASE OF THE WEEK IS RULED OUT ON LICENCE, AND IT IS A REGRESSION FROM WHAT IS ALREADY INSTALLED. Black Forest Labs shipped FLUX 3 Image Klein on 13-14 October across four repos, and the ComfyUI one has 338,036 downloads in 30 days and 835 likes — the most-adopted new image release this report has seen. Every repo that contains an image model is `license: other` / `flux-kommunity-license` with `gated: auto`: flux-3-image-klein (43.32 GB, 5.55B BF16), flux-3-image-klein-base (43.23 GB), flux-3-image-klein-comfy (93.72 GB). Per the licence rule in docs/models.md that is a bespoke vendor licence and waits in notes until a human reads it — the gate is only a click-through and is not the problem; the terms are. AND NOTE WHAT THAT MEANS HERE SPECIFICALLY: config/model-meta.json records local-flux2-klein-4b as Apache-2.0, so adopting FLUX 3 Klein would trade an Apache-2.0 model for a bespoke-licensed one in the same family. WHAT IS WORTH KNOWING IF SOMEONE DOES READ THOSE TERMS. The Comfy repack ships an NVFP4 build of the denoiser at 5,277,685,632 B, which sm_120 executes in hardware on BeTenshi and which will not load on B5 at all — the cleanest two-machine split in the lane. It also ships int8-convrot at 5.83 GB against bf16's 11.10 GB. THE REAL COST IS NOT THE DENOISER: the README states flatly that 'FLUX 3 Image Klein is not meant to run without a prompt upsampler in front of it, for text-to-image, editing and layout alike; a short prompt sent to the image model as typed gives generic output'. That upsampler is black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup, a full fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B at 18,819,722,392 B bf16 — and it is the one repo in the set that IS apache-2.0 and ungated, because Qwen3.5-9B is. So the honest footprint of a FLUX 3 Klein setup is an image model plus a 9B VLM, 18.82 GB bf16 or 6.72 GB at the shipped w4a8 rung, and on a 31.8 GB card that is the binding constraint, not the 5.28 GB denoiser. On B5's 128 GB pool the whole stack is unremarkable, and B5 has no ComfyUI to put it in.

HiDream-ai publishes fourteen repos and none is a 1.5; a Hub-wide search for 'HiDream' sorted by last-modified returns only third-party mirrors, ONNX conversions and quantisations of the EXISTING O1. So the arena has scored something that is not downloadable from the place this console downloads from, and there is nothing to recommend — watch HiDream-ai for a 1.5 release and take it the week it lands. TWO MACHINES, and this week the asymmetry is about PACKAGING rather than memory. Every speech candidate is 4.09 to 6.76 GB with portable weights and no `runtimes` pin, so fit arithmetic separates nothing between the boxes. Both image candidates fit both machines on size: MOSS-Image at 13.01 GB (int8+w4a8) or 29.81 GB (bf16) and Iris-3B at 14.86 GB (turbo) or 20.84 GB (full) are all inside BeTenshi's 31.8 GB card and trivial in B5's 128 GB pool. WHAT ACTUALLY DECIDES IT IS THAT ONLY BETENSHI HAS COMFYUI. config/hosts/betenshi.json lists a comfyui service on :8188 and nine of the image and video models in config/model-meta.json are Comfy-Org repacks loaded through it; config/hosts/b5.json lists three services — manager, ollama and a qwen adapter — and its image path is Draw Things. So a Comfy-Org repack is a file copy on BeTenshi and a new service on B5, which is why MOSS-Image is recommended for BeTenshi and merely noted for B5. NO `runtimes` IS SET ON EITHER IMAGE CANDIDATE and that is deliberate per rule 5: MOSS-Image's bf16 safetensors are diffusers-portable even though the vendor documents a CUDA quick start, and Iris-3B is plain safetensors plus a Qwen3-VL encoder. The rungs are where the hardware shows: MOSS-Image's w4a8_gptq encoder is GPTQ, which runtimesFor() reads as CUDA-or-ROCm and not Metal, and int8-convrot is a Comfy-side quant — so the 13.01 GB set is BeTenshi-shaped and B5 would take the 29.81 GB bf16 set, which it has room for. FLUX 3 Klein's NVFP4 build, if its licence is ever cleared, is the hard case: sm_120 only, and B5 cannot load it at any size.

THE FOLLOW-ON NOBODY HAS DONE YET, unchanged for six weeks and still the cheapest win on BeTenshi, stated once more because it is a deletion rather than a download. local-flux-schnell and local-qwen-image are both still in config/model-meta.json and both were REJECTED by admission control during the 12 September experiment — schnell on its measured 31.72 GiB VRAM / 28 GB host RAM peak, Qwen-Image on its 28 GB RAM estimate against 28.94 GB available. local-qwen-image's own footprint basis spells out why it is the expensive one: idleRamGb EQUALS ramGb at 28 GB, because enable_model_cpu_offload() keeps the fp8 weights in host RAM for as long as the service is loaded, and 'that standing 28 GB is what collides with a FLUX run on a 63 GB box'. Any new image model admitted to that card is competing with a standing 28 GB that nothing is generating with. On B5's unified pool the same model costs one copy rather than two and this whole paragraph does not apply — which is the clearest example on the page of why evaluateFit() branches on memoryModel.

PARAMETER COUNT IS STILL NOT THE FOOTPRINT, and this week gives four fresh examples and one new shape. MOSS-Image publishes 5,082,308,624 params; 5,082,308,624 x 2 = 10,164,617,248 against a transformer directory of 10,164,655,808 B, so the count covers the DiT and EXCLUDES a text encoder of 16.79 GB (diffusers repo) or 19.31 GB (Comfy repack) — the published number describes 37% of the download. Iris-3B publishes 2,987,511,888 params at exactly 4.0000 bytes each, correctly describing an fp32 denoiser, and silently omits the 8.89 GB Qwen3-VL-4B encoder its own config names — the mistake this report made. FLUX 3 Image Klein publishes 5.55B and needs an 18.82 GB 9B upsampler to produce anything but generic output. TheStageAI/thewhisper-large-v3-turbo publishes 808,878,080 params and ships 74.67 GB, because the repo is a matrix of compiled engines per GPU. THE NEW SHAPE IS THE SAME REPO HOLDING SEVERAL COMPLETE MODELS: iris-3b is 41.91 GB over four directories that are four full fine-tunes of one prior — root, depth, upscaler and now turbo — so a naive snapshot download costs 2.8x what any single use needs, and the right move is always one directory. Both AuK repos publish NO parameter count at all, so estimateFromParams() must not be run on them; the leaderboard's 1.53B against 6.76 GB of weights would be 4.4 bytes/param and therefore describes one component.

TEXT LLMs ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THE CANDIDATES, per rule 4. The Leaderboard tab ranks every open-weights text model with a published parameter count against the live card automatically, and cloud discovery carries live prices — a hand-written candidate there would go stale beside data that does not. This report's only contributions in the text lane are the gpt-5.5, gemini-flash, gemini-pro and three Claude repoints above, which discovery structurally cannot make because familyKey() cannot see that 'terra' is a tier name or that argon is a generation.
